subject: Sealed facility readiness — spares kit, offline patch windows & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Matthew Cooper <matthew@calyxtx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Sealed facility readiness — spares kit, offline patch windows & next steps

Hi Matthew — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) High-level agreement from the call
- Calyx is leaning toward a Private (air-gapped) deployment inside the sealed facility for PHI-handling workloads; Backup path is Dedicated for burst/maintenance windows.
- You need confirmation on minimum serviceable spares, patch cadence options (monthly vs quarterly), and an offline patch playbook for auditors.

2) Attachments we’re sending with this thread (first pass)
- RI_Spares_Kit_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — recommended spare parts and suggested quantities.
- sealed-site-patch-playbook.pdf — draft offline patch workflow and rollback steps.

3) Action items (owners + timelines)
- Matthew / Calyx procurement: confirm if on-site inventory can store 2-week spares (by 2028-05-26).
- Karthik (SE): provide an updated BOM for the air-gapped appliance including spares SKU and lead times (by 2028-05-24).
- Laura (Security): capture any additional evidence items you need for your internal auditors — we can add them to the playbook (by 2028-05-25).
- Marissa / Sales: prepare simple fallback SLA language for Dedicated during maintenance (by 2028-05-27).

4) Scheduling
- Proposed offline patch window: Sundays 02:00–06:00 local (we suggested this on the call). If that conflicts with your ops, let us know alternatives.

If this looks accurate I’ll mark the tasks in the deal and loop in procurement thread (procurement@calyxtx.com). Thanks — appreciate the clarity on requirements.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments: RI_Spares_Kit_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), sealed-site-patch-playbook.pdf (document)

From: Matthew Cooper <matthew@calyxtx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@calyxtx.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sealed facility readiness — spares kit, offline patch windows & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the write-up, looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Hardware spares: we can allocate a small locked cabinet in the utility room, but inventory must be limited to critical spares only. The 2-week spare recommendation might be over-provisioned for us; can you confirm a minimal kit (72-hour) we can start with?
- Patch window: Sundays 02:00–06:00 is acceptable, but our ops lead asked if a 2-hour “hotfix” channel could be used for critical security fixes outside the window — we’d need to understand the fallbacks to Dedicated for short bursts.
- Audit artifacts: will need a single consolidated PDF of the playbook and a change log template we can keep in our records.

Also looped procurement to start POs if we agree on minimal spares SKU numbers.

—Matthew
Matthew Cooper
IT Operations Manager | Calyx Therapeutics
matthew@calyxtx.com
+1 (617) 555-3344

Thanks — quick technical follow-up from my side: 

- Minimal 72-hour spares kit (recommended) — I trimmed the spreadsheet to a minimal SKU set and updated expected lead times in the attached workbook. Key items: 1 spare NVMe node, 1 spare power module, 2x fan modules, 1 spare NIC module, and basic cable kit. Lead times for the NVMe node are currently 4–6 weeks; we can ship faster as a rush order but it increases cost.
- Hotfix channel and Dedicated fallback: we can support a 2-hour emergency maintenance path provided Calyx signals via the emergency contact (outlined in the playbook). During those 2 hours we can route traffic to your Dedicated reserve (if you procure it) or pause non-essential workloads. I’ll add an explicit decision tree to the playbook showing traffic routing and failure modes.
- Change log template: added to sealed-site-patch-playbook.pdf as an appendix and saved a simple CSV template in the Drive link.

Next steps from technical side:
- I’ll send an updated spreadsheet (minimal kit) by EOD with per-item SKU and estimated cost.
- If Calyx can confirm storage constraints (cabinet dimensions), I’ll validate the physical packing for the spare kit.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: RI_Spares_Kit_v1.xlsx (updated minimal tab)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Matthew Cooper <matthew@calyxtx.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Sealed facility readiness — spares kit, offline patch windows & next steps

Appended a short security checklist for the auditors — please confirm if you want this as part of the playbook PDF or a separate evidence pack. Highlights: 

- Inventory chain-of-custody: recommend a weekly signed log for any spares removed from the cabinet.
- Firmware validation: all spare modules must be fingerprinted (SHA256) before being deployed; include the fingerprint in the change log.
- Patch audit trail: require a signed pre/post checklist for each offline patch window with timestamps and operator IDs.

If Calyx prefers, we can produce an "evidence bundle" (single PDF) with the checklist, change log template, and RI playbook for upload to your auditors.

Laura Bennett
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura@redwoodinference.com
